answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it earns reputation: for example, complete a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test, with failure forfeiting the bond. A copper ledger records bonds and outcomes; sable marks unresolved cases, and a jetty of independent reviewers handles disputes. Spawning a thousand Sybils then means funding and risking a thousand bonds, not merely minting usernames; the attacker also pays for real task work and cannot cheaply recycle failed identities.
